title: TANGO: Humanoid Navigation in Cluttered Environments with a Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Model
why_read: A concrete robotics paper showing a vision-language-action model controlling a full-body humanoid for navigation through clutter, with real hardware deployment.
analysis: TANGO is a whole-body control system for humanoid robots that combines natural language instructions with vision to navigate cluttered spaces, predicting joint actions across 29 degrees of freedom rather than just planning a 2D path. It's trained purely in simulation using synthesized motion data and then deployed zero-shot onto a real Unitree G1 humanoid, which is a meaningful sim-to-real result. This matters technically because most navigation research treats robots as points moving on a floor plan, while this approach handles arms, torso, and gait together for genuine obstacle negotiation. The zero-shot real-world transfer without real navigation training data is a notable engineering achievement.
